text:
olivia: Quick idea: instead of fsyncing a manifest per-shard or hammering catalog CAS, what about a local append-only activation journal per node? append intent records, fsync batches, then publish a compacted activation checkpoint to the catalog. replayable and bounded.

sam: Interesting. journal = single write stream per node, lower fsync pressure if we batch. How do we make replay idempotent if partial activations happened before crash?

nate: design: each journal record = {lsn, shard_id, range_start, range_end, phase, checksum}. On replay we scan journal up to last durable LSN and reconcile: if payloads exist on disk and checksum matches, mark activated. else re-stream. Idempotent if our streaming writes are deterministic and checksummed.

daria: Concern: journal becomes another state machine to maintain. Need compaction/GC. Proposal: compact-to-checkpoint periodically: atomically write a checkpoint blob to catalog (with latest LSN) then truncate journal locally. Catalog holds authoritative checkpoint LSN.

olivia: Exactly. benefits: we avoid CAS hotpath for every activation bump, and catalog only gets periodic consolidated checkpoints. Also easier to correlate per-node streaming progress.

sam: What about cross-node coordination? If two nodes handle shards for same model, their checkpoints must be comparable. We can namespace checkpoints per-node+model, catalog stores per-node checkpoint LSNs. Global readiness computed by rollout controller collecting node LSNs.

nate: Failure modes: if node writes journal, fsyncs, then dies before streaming payloads finish, other nodes must not rely on that node's checkpoint until payloads actually materialize. Use phases: INTENT -> MATERIALIZING -> COMPLETE. INTENT and MATERIALIZING are visible for debugging but not for readiness.

daria: Ops: We must surface metrics: journal_bytes_written, outstanding_intents, last_compact_lsn, replay_duration. Also trace spans: warmup.journal.append and warmup.journal.replay.

olivia: Implementation notes: lightweight C++ journal writer using O_APPEND, buffered batch fsyncs every N intents or every T ms. Keep per-shard in-memory index of activated ranges (tiny). Streaming still chunked (e.g., 2MB chunks) and writes verify xxhash64.

sam: Security: journal contains shard ids and ranges - sensitive? It doesn't contain model weights. Still, encrypt journal at rest (node disk) or allow customers to opt-out of persistent journal and fall back to catalog-only atomic approach.

nate: Integration with eviction: if an eviction removes a shard mid-stream, journal will have MATERIALIZING entries; on replay we detect missing payload and re-trigger stream. Also we can use journal to resume where we left off rather than restart from zero.

daria: Latency tradeoff: batching fsync reduces overhead but increases short window where an activation is durable only in-memory. But since we don't advertise COMPLETE until fsync+write of COMPLETE marker, clients won't see it. So safe.

olivia: sample journal entry format (text log for prototype):

```
LSN:12345,SHARD:models/mistral/1,PHASE:INTENT,START:0,END:1048576,CHK:0x9ab3
LSN:12346,SHARD:models/mistral/1,PHASE:MATERIALIZING,CHUNK:0,BYTES:1048576,CHK:0x9ab3
LSN:12347,SHARD:models/mistral/1,PHASE:COMPLETE,LSN_CHECK:12346
```

sam: Nice. That text format is easy to debug; for prod we'll use compact binary with checks.

nate: Edge-case: simultaneous rollout + compaction. Ensure compaction writes checkpoint with inclusive LSN and only truncates journal up to that LSN after ensuring checkpoint persisted in catalog. Use two-phase commit with catalog ack.

daria: Ops ask: add an alert when journal grows beyond threshold (suspected stuck streaming) and when replay time > threshold. Also add a rollout-killer if too many nodes stuck.

olivia: Perf numbers estimate: batching fsync every 50 intents or 200ms gives <1% CPU overhead plus ~4-8ms amortized fsync per-batch on nvme. We'll measure.

sam: POC plan: implement node journal writer + replay harness, wire into existing warmup flow, expose metrics, run chaos test (kill during MATERIALIZING). ETA: POC 5d.

nate: I'll add replay correctness tests to the warmup suite. also test resume-from-LSN on partial-chunk write corruption.

daria: Action items:
- olivia: write mini-RFC describing journal checkpoint flow + compaction (ETA 2d)
- sam: implement prototype journal writer and metrics (ETA 5d)
- nate: tests + chaos scenarios (ETA 3d)
- daria: observability + alerts (ETA 2d)

ops-bot: nightly-run: warmup-journal-smoke passed 8/8 :white_check_mark:
